newsitem.title: SUDAN: Sudan condemns rebel fighting in south.
newsitem.headline: Sudan condemns rebel fighting in south.

text.p: A senior Sudanese official on Tuesday acknowledged that rebels of the Sudan People's Liberation Army (SPLA) had attacked towns in Buheirat state but did not confirm the group's claims that it captured two towns.
"The fighting started by John Garang's (SPLA) forces in Bahr el-Ghazal area is meaningless and unjustifiable," said Mohammad al-Amin Khalifa, secretary-general of the Supreme Council for Peace.

Buheirat state is one of a number of states in Bahr el-Ghazal area. The SPLA, led by John Garang, said it had captured the town of Tonj in Buheirat state last week and was advancing towards the district headquarters at Wau in southern Sudan.

The SPLA also said it had captured Buheirat state capital Rumbek, 70 km (45 miles) southeast of Tonj in April. The rebels said they captured several state ministers and members of the state parliament in Rumbek.
Khalifa's comments, carried on the official news agency SUNA, were the first government reference to fighting in Buheirat state.
"By launching a war following the realisation of peace, Garang's group is proving its insistence on killing citizens and causing panic among innocent people," Khalifa said.

He was referring to a peace treaty the government signed recently in Khartoum with several southern Sudanese groups who were formerly linked with the SPLA. Garang's movement had denounced the agreement.

The SPLA has recently claimed a string of successes further south, near the Uganda border, including the capture of Yei, a key town near the Uganda and Zaire borders. But the key city of Juba, on the Nile, remains in government hands.
